newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch unveil draft treaty for EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Dutch unveil draft treaty for EU summit.

text.p: The European Union unveiled a draft treaty on Thursday making job creation a prime focus of EU activities and offering its citizens a broad range of freedoms in a secure and just continent.

It also called for the bloc to streamline its decision making, achieve greater clout on the world stage, and set out a framework for the EU's keenest integrationists to move ahead of others if they wish.

The draft, to be considered by EU leaders at a summit in Amsterdam on Monday and Tuesday, is the culmination of 15 months of negotiation designed to prepare the bloc for enlargement into eastern Europe.

Among its proposals -- all subject to veto by any EU member state at the summit -- are the eventual integration of the Western European Union defence grouping into the bloc and the incorporation of the Schengen border-free pact.
Britain and Ireland would be given an opt-out and be allowed to keep their border checks with the rest of the Union.
The draft treaty also conserves the right of EU countries to a European commissioner, something demanded by small states, but gives larger countries relatively more power in decision making.
